title: The Soviet Bloc and China's Runtime Version Transition
summary: The early Cold War produced more than competition between two states; it also expanded different institutional blocs. The Soviet bloc developed cross-border political and economic coordination, while the People's Republic of China built a new state runtime and later underwent further version transitions.

blocks.text: The early Cold War produced more than competition between two states; it also expanded different institutional blocs. The Soviet bloc developed cross-border political and economic coordination, while the People's Republic of China built a new state runtime and later underwent further version transitions.

The article observes institutional structure and version change without collapsing different societies into a single ideological label or ranking political systems. The common question is how states establish, maintain and revise their modes of coordination.

This article distinguishes historical fact, historical reconstruction and structural interpretation in the manuscript. Later outcomes are not treated as inevitable at the time, and motives or causal claims not present in the manuscript are not added.
